newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: The bond market ended on a positive note on Tuesday as local institutional and offshore buying steered yields to their best levels in two weeks.
But volumes were thin with little in the form of direction to entice large buyers into the market, dealers said.
The key R150 was last quoted at a 15.205 percent after touching a day's best level of 15.195 percent shortly before the 1400 GMT finish and from 15.30 percent overnight.

"We've seen some good buying out of London and the local institutions on the back of slightly stronger U.S. bonds and the steady rand," a dealer said. "But volumes have been thin and it might have been a bit of an exaggerated move."
Dealers noted, however, that while the market lacked any fundamental direction, technical indicators pointed to further strength in the market.
"We've broken a couple of levels and technically we are looking quite strong," one trader said.
"At the moment we have to close below 15.185 percent before we are in a bull market, but we are getting closer," another trader added.
With no domestic economic indicators scheduled for release this week, dealers said they would look to September U.S. CPI data which is released on Wednesday at 1230 GMT for direction.
On the currency market, the rand ended unchanged against the dollar in trade described as two-way but thin.
It was last quoted at 4.5390/5440 -- unmoved from its late Monday level.
"We saw a bit of two-way trade, but volumes were very thin again," a dealer said. "There has not been much action at all today."
The rand remained under pressure against the British pound, however, as sterling continued to gain ground against the dollar, Deutschmark and yen.

It touched a new all-time low of 7.1936 against sterling earlier in the day before retracing to 7.1816/1941 at the close. Against the mark, the rand improved as the dollar strengthened against the German currency. It was last trading at 0.3388/3392 from 0.3364/3370.

On the money market, three-month NCDs ticked up to between 15.85 percent and 16.00 percent from 15.80 and 16.00 percent on Monday, while 90-day BAs were also unchanged a touch higher at between 15.30 and 15.40 percent from 15.25 to 15.40 percent.
The daily shortage was quoted at 7.940 billion rand on Monday from 8.103 billion rand on Saturday.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners sold a net 147.58 million rand worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying a net 99.69 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to a paltry 2.46 billion rand on Monday from 5.16 billion rand on Friday.
